summary:
Fixes to the built-ins, for keyboards, screen readers and right-to-left
pages. Nothing a project writes changes.

items.text:
**A `Switch` can be reached from the keyboard and is heard as a switch.**
Its input was `display: none`, which took the very element that says
"switch" and "on" out of the Tab order and the accessibility tree. It is
now laid unseen over the control, with a focus ring on the track.

**A `Sidebar` shut off a narrow page is out of the Tab order.** It was
only slid aside, so Tab walked through links no one could see. It is
hidden once it has slid out, and opening it from its toggle takes the
focus to its first link.

**A press on a `Modal`'s or a `Dialog`'s backdrop closes it**, and its
`visible:` state follows, as a press outside a popover or a menu
already did. A press inside, or a selection dragged out of it, does not.

**A toast shown while a modal is open is seen and heard.** It was drawn
under the modal, which also made it inert. The stack is now drawn in the
top layer and moves into the open modal for as long as it is open.

**The first message is heard.** The live regions that toasts, route
changes and form errors speak through were made on their first message,
which a screen reader does not announce. They are made when the page
loads. A form error is no longer said twice.

`Tabs`, menus and a `Splitter` follow the page's direction: in an Arabic
page ArrowLeft moves to the next tab, opens a submenu, and widens the
region before a splitter. A submenu opens to the left of its item, and a
layer placed `.bottomStart` lines up with its anchor's right edge.

A `Carousel` moves to the next slide in the right direction, a `Switch`'s
thumb slides the right way, and toasts come in from the page's end.

Arrow keys pressed with Alt, Ctrl or ⌘ are left to the browser, so
Alt+ArrowLeft goes back from a tab strip or a menu.

An async action's `pending` stays true until every call of it has ended;
the first of two calls to end used to clear it while the second ran.

`show` with an exit animation no longer hides content that was shown
again before the exit ended.

A `Splitter`'s handle reaches 24px, WCAG 2.2's least target, around its
4px line.

summary:
A site sends much less: the runtime ships only the functions a program
reaches, with short names, and only the styles and animations it draws
on. The compiler draws icons and the reader's theme before any script
runs, and refuses a few more programs that built and then failed in the
browser. A project that builds with 6.0 builds with 6.1 unless `wf check`
now finds one of those (see "Upgrading").

sections.title: Smaller
sections.intro:
Gzipped, built by 6.0.0 and by 6.1.0 from the same sources:

| Project | `app.js` | `styles.css` |
|---|---|---|
| The counter example | 9.2 → 4.2 kB | 3.8 → 1.9 kB |
| `wf init -t static` | 23.7 → 14.8 kB | 5.5 → 4.3 kB |
| `wf init -t spa` | 23.9 → 16.9 kB | 6.2 → 5.0 kB |
| The documentation site (564 pages) | 142 → 111 kB | 16.7 → 15.8 kB |

items.text:
**The runtime is cut by function, not by module.** One call into a
module used to ship all of it, and every function of `core` shipped to
every project. A build now keeps what runs at load, every function the
program calls through `WF`, and what those name, until nothing new is
named; `WF` exports only what is called. A project's own scripts, an
`elements` build's definitions, the dev server's stores panel and the
studio count as callers. `"build": { "runtime": "full" }` still ships
everything.

**The runtime's names are shortened** in a minified build: its
top-level functions and values, and each function's locals, the most
used first. What a program calls on `WF` keeps its name.

**Only the styles a project draws on.** The grid, columns, spacers,
dividers, code highlighting, Markdown, drag and drop, and the document
and slide elements are each kept only with the component that uses
them, and the rules every page keeps (reflow, focus, reduced motion)
lose the selectors of components a project does not use.

**Only the motion a project uses.** The animation module ships to a
program that animates: an animation, an element marked to enter or
leave, or a router transition. The route-transition player and async
validation ship only when used; key combinations and the theme are
modules of their own.
**A one-page site is one file**: its code is in `app.js`, with no chunk.

**A route table without the pages' details.** A split build sends each
page's title, language and layout with the page's own chunk, so
`app.js` holds only each route's path and page name.

**`wf build --stats`** counts what the build keeps of each runtime
module, and what that comes to with its names shortened.

sections.after:
A build does more to prune, so it takes a few milliseconds longer on a
small project (about 8% on the documentation site).

items.text:
**Icons in the static paint.** Every built-in icon is drawn into the
pre-rendered HTML, from the same table the runtime draws it from.
Before, an icon was an empty element until the script ran, so a
header's icon buttons were blank squares on the first paint.

**The reader's theme before the first paint.** A site that calls
`setTheme` gets a small `theme.js`, linked first, which puts the
reader's choice on the page before it is drawn: no flash of the other
theme.

**A page's own language in its text.** A page with `lang:` shows its
`t()` text from that language's table, in the pre-render and while it
shows; leaving it puts back the reader's language.

**A call at the top of `app` is set-up code**, run once when the site
opens: `app { use Session  Session.load()  Router }`. It was read as an
element with a flag.

**One `main` landmark.** A program that draws its own `main` (an
element with `role: "main"`) gets a plain `div` as the box the router
draws pages into, so a page has one main landmark and its header is a
top-level banner. The box keeps its `id`, `wf-main`.

**One skip link.** The engine's own skip link is left out when a page
opens with its own.

**A Markdown code block takes keyboard focus** (`<pre tabindex="0">`),
built and live, so a long line can be scrolled without a mouse.

**`reduce` and `reduceRight` at build time**, so a `derived` value
folded with them shows in the static paint, a template and `wf test`.

**The browser compiler's preview without a service worker.**
`previewInline()` in `crates/wf-wasm/wf.js` serves a build through
`run.html` where a browser refuses a service worker (a private window,
some embedded browsers).

**`T10`: an endpoint called with positional arguments.**
`Backend.signUp(email, password)` sent the first value as the call's
map and the second nowhere; the finding writes the call by name.

**`E111` in `wf check`: a theme the config names and the program does
not declare.** `wf build` stopped on it while `wf check` said "No
problems".

**`R05` reads the site's language.** A page with no `lang:` is in
`meta.lang`, so a translation written in that language is now caught.
**`log(a, b)`** says `log` takes one value and how to log several.

A component or store member only a `test` reaches is no longer `U03`
or `U04`; a `t()` key a string elsewhere in the program names is no
longer unused.

**`optimistic()` works.** It was handed the state's value instead of
the state, and threw `holder is not a function` every time. An action
that used it without awaiting anything was written with `await` in a
plain function, which stopped the page; and a store's action never
rolled back what it showed.

**A variant or a size given state follows it.** `Button("Save", tone:
tone)` and `Stack(gap: gap)` wrote the value as an attribute nothing
reads, so the element kept its default look. A class prop (and `gap`,
`align`, `justify`) that reads state is now a class looked up from its
case, followed as the state changes and painted at its first value.

**A short token as a value.** `state accent = $primary` compiled to
`var(--primary)`, which no theme sets; a short name only one token
group has is that group's (`$color-primary`).

**`wf verify` is ten times faster**: a page is done once it has loaded
and been quiet for 100 ms (900 ms at most), and up to three browsers
visit a site's routes at once.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Run `wf check`. It may find `T10` (call an endpoint by name), `E111` (a
theme the config names that no file declares) or `R05` (a page and its
translation both in the site's language: set `meta.lang`, or give the
page `lang:`). A stylesheet that selects `main#wf-main` should select
`#wf-main` when the program draws its own `main`.

summary:
A page can be in a language of its own, the compiler holds up to anything
it is given, and the Rust library has a smaller surface with typed errors.
A project that builds with 5.14 builds with 6.0, unless it relied on
something now refused because it shipped a broken page (a status code the
grammar cannot hold, nesting past 100 levels). What 6.0 breaks on purpose
is the Rust API (see "Upgrading").

items.text:
**`lang:` on a page.** `page HomeEn(path: "/en", lang: "en", …)` is
written `<html lang="en">` (and `dir="rtl"` for a language written right
to left), with its own `og:locale` and `inLanguage` on its JSON-LD
`WebPage`. The router sets `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` when it shows the
page, and puts back the site's language, or the locale the reader chose,
on a page without one. `wf render` uses it when no `--lang` is given. A
site whose pages declared one language each used to ship every page in
`meta.lang`, so crawlers and link previews read its English pages as
Arabic (#6).

**`translates:` on a page.** `translates: Home` names the page this one
is a translation of. Pages joined this way, directly or through each
other, list each other as `hreflang` alternates, each at its own address,
canonical to itself and in its own `lang:`, with `x-default` for the one
in the site's language, and name each other's languages as
`og:locale:alternate`. A `:param` page's translation is matched by its
parameters (`/en/posts/:slug` for `/posts/:slug`).

**`R05`**: a `translates:` that names no page or its own, or two
translations of one page in one language.

**`worker` is offered where a statement starts**, beside `socket`,
`stream`, `channel` and `peer`.

sections.title: Faster
sections.intro:
Measured on the documentation site (77 files, 140 pages); `cargo xtask
bench` reproduces the numbers.

items.text: **`wf build` takes 0.36 s instead of 4.4 s**, to the same bytes:
points: pages are painted, compressed and read back on every core;

a `data` constant is shared rather than copied each time a page reads
it;

the compressor finds its matches faster, and is run once a file rather
than twice;

items.text: **`wf check` takes 62 ms instead of 82.**
**The language server answers in about 0.1 ms instead of 46:**
points:
it keeps the analysed project between requests, and analyses it again
only after a change;
an unchanged file keeps its parse and its tokens.
items.after:
An edit's findings arrive in 74 ms instead of 145. Before, a hover cost
as much as checking the whole project and grew with it.

items.text:
**No more `?lang=` alternates.** A project with several `i18n.locales`
listed `?lang=<code>` for each as an `hreflang` alternate, but every
`?lang=` address serves the default locale's HTML with the bare address
as its canonical, so a search engine filed each one as a duplicate and
ignored the set (#5). A locale the browser switches to on one address is
not an alternate; translations with `translates:` are. `?lang=` still
opens a page in that locale for a reader who follows such a link.

**The compiler cannot be made to hang or crash by what it reads.** A
name starting with a letter such as `℘` no longer loops forever; nesting
past 100 levels is `E120` instead of a stack overflow; a template render
is bounded (`E121`); the parser and the PDF engine return an error for
input they cannot read rather than panicking; a picture is refused past
50 megapixels before it is decoded.

**Names in any script repaint.** A state named in Arabic (`state عدد`)
is reactive in the bundle, and a name may start with any letter Unicode
allows in an identifier.

**Text is written as text.** A `\` or `${` in a spliced string, a page
title, a class or a colour from data, a `head { }` tag and a
`Frame` are escaped where they are written, and the build reads its own
pages back as a browser would before it ships them. A template's data
cannot add CSS declarations or attributes.

**`Template` answers as `wf build` does**: one evaluator and one
renderer serve both, so `name.length`, comparisons and indexing agree.

**A page's state no longer leaks into `app`**, and a rendering server
that catches a panic no longer carries one render's state into the next.

**Every parse error is reported**, not only the first; findings are in a
fixed order and placed by character, not byte.

**Numbers the grammar cannot hold are refused** (a status past 599, a
fractional one, a negative carousel interval) instead of being clamped.
**`.wfx` lexing is linear** in the size of the file.

**Builds stay in their project.** `build.output` outside the project is
refused unless `--allow-output-outside` says so, `wf serve` listens on
this machine unless `--host` says otherwise and serves nothing outside
the build, and a `public_env` name takes no value from the shell unless
`WF_ALLOW_SHELL_ENV` names it.

**`wf verify` and `wf test`** run Chrome with its sandbox, in a private
profile that goes when `wf` does.

**I/O errors name their file**, and a config or translation that is there
but cannot be read is an error rather than the defaults.
SVG text is laid out with the document's own fonts.

**`wf check --allow-output-outside`**, as `wf build` has: a project whose
`build.output` is outside it could not be checked at all.

The grammars read names in any script, raw strings of any length and two
declarations on one style line as the compiler does.

Zed colours `worker` and `expect not`, outlines parts and persisted state,
and has snippets for `persist`, `validate`, `on key`, `api` and `test`.

VS Code colours every style property, colour and regex literals, a
splice's format, `///` and `// wf-allow(…)`, and the indented layout's
blocks.

The language server reads the compiler's own tables for keywords, events,
built-in names and design tokens, and follows a component's props, events
and slots for definitions and renames.

Both extensions download the release they pin and check it against
`SHA256SUMS`.

VS Code colours a name in any script as the compiler reads one, and
tells a member (`e.message`) from a flag (`.danger`).
The grammars read a raw string inside code that does not parse yet.

**One documented surface.** `template`, `syntax` (the AST, `fmt`,
`layout`), `diagnostics`, `build`, `config`, `vfs`, `outfs`, `memory`,
`init`, `studio` and the root items are the API semver covers.

**The rest is the crate's own**: the checker, the code generator, the PDF
engine, the registry and the tools. The `internals` feature makes them
public again, hidden from the docs and outside semver, for a tool that
accepts that they change in any release.

**One path per item.** The root's second paths (`webfluent::lexer`,
`::parser`, `::fmt`, `::error`, `::assets`, …) are gone; use the layer's
(`webfluent::syntax::fmt`, `webfluent::diagnostics::error`).

**One finding type.** The linters and the studio return
`diagnostics::Diagnostic`; `A11yWarning`, `VocabWarning` and
`studio::StudioDiagnostic` are gone (`rule_id` is `code`).

**Typed errors.** `WebFluentError::IoError`, `ConfigError`,
`CodegenError`, `EditError` and `NotFound` hold their own types, each a
message and the error beneath it, which `source()` walks. Build one with
`WebFluentError::io(…)`, or `io_with(message, cause)` to keep the cause;
`?` on an `io::Error` keeps it too. What an error prints is unchanged.

**`#[non_exhaustive]`** on `WebFluentError`, the AST's enums that gain
cases (`Declaration`, `Expr`, `StatementKind`, `TypeRef`, `Step`, …),
`Plan`, `Tag`, `OutputType`, `RuntimeMode`, `ScriptLoad`,
`init::Template`, `memory::Contents`, `EditOp` and `ArgRef`.

**Dependencies are up to date**: every crate at its newest release the
crate's Rust version accepts, `taffy` 0.15 and `miniz_oxide` 0.9 among
them. `usvg` 0.47 and `fontdb` 0.23 stay where `krilla-svg` holds them.

**A project:** nothing to change. A multilingual site that relied on the
`?lang=` alternates had them ignored by search engines already; to have
each language indexed, give it pages of its own with `lang:` and
`translates:`.
**A program using the crate:**
points:
a path that no longer resolves moved to its layer
(`webfluent::fmt` → `webfluent::syntax::fmt`);
a `match` on an enum above needs a `_` arm;

items.text: **The editors** pin this release: update the extension after it is out.

summary:
The compiler runs in a browser. Built for WebAssembly, it does in a page
what `wf build` does on a machine — sites and apps, every check, pictures
sized to WebP, PDFs and slide decks — with nothing sent to a server. It is
what the documentation's playground runs.

items.text:
**The compiler as WebAssembly** (`crates/wf-wasm`). `wf.js` is the one
thing a page imports: `compile(files, config)` takes a project as a map
of path to text or bytes and gives back the files the build wrote, its
pictures and PDFs, and every finding exactly as `wf check --format json`
lists them; `check`, `explain` and `registerFont` beside it. A demo page
compiles as you type.

**Loaded by what a project needs.** The compiler is about 1.6 MB
gzipped, fetched on the first call. A project whose config asks for a PDF
or a deck loads a second build with the paged engine (about 2.7 MB) and
the fonts it is set in, then and only then; a face for Arabic is fetched
the first time a document has Arabic in it, since a browser has no
machine fonts to fall back on.

**A preview served as a host would serve it.** `preview(out)` hands a
build to a service worker that answers for it under `preview/` — every
page, chunk, stylesheet and picture, and the routes between them.

**Pictures in the browser.** libwebp is compiled to WebAssembly against
a C library of its own, so a picture is sized and written as WebP as
`wf build` does it; the encodings are kept from one build to the next,
so an edit that leaves the picture alone does not encode it again.

**`webfluent::memory`**: `compile` and `compile_files` build a project
from memory — no disk read, none written — with the findings and the
output as values. It runs natively as well.

**`webfluent::outfs`** is where a build writes: the disk, or memory
inside `outfs::capture`. **`webfluent::platform`** stands in for
threads, clocks and the environment where WebAssembly has none.

`OverlayVfs::set_bytes` lays a file that is not text (a picture, a
font) over a path.

The paged engine reads a project's fonts and pictures through the
`Vfs` it is given (`Options::from_pdf_via`, `from_slides_via`,
`reader_via`), and `paged::fonts::register_font` takes a face — a font
file as it is, zlib or gzip — that stands where a built-in one does.

Three features for a WebAssembly build: `webp`, `pdf` and
`bundled-fonts`. A native build has all three whatever the features
say, so `default-features = false` leaves PDFs and WebP as they were.

**A `style { }` on a component's call styles the component.** Its rule
was compiled and its class put on nothing, so placing a component in a
grid or sizing it from its call did nothing. The class now joins the
root's classes, as `class:` does, on the live page and in the static
paint.

**An `if let` value whose branch awaits compiles.** `if let p = x {
await f(p) } else { … }` used as a value made a plain arrow with an
`await` in it, and the page's code did not parse; it is now an async
arrow, awaited.

**D01 reads `public/` through the project's `Vfs`**, as every other
check does, so an editor's unsaved picture or a project held in memory
counts as there.

**An `@font-face` in a PDF is read from its bytes**, not written to a
temporary file first.

**The agents' skill says which compiler it is for.** `just bump` now
sets the skill's version and its copy of `AGENTS.md` with the crates,
and the release preflight refuses a skill left behind. 5.13.0 shipped
saying 5.12.0.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Nothing to change. A project builds to the same bytes as it did with
5.13.0.

summary:
WebFluent for coding agents: a skill that teaches the `wf` loop, a
reference with a part written for agents, and a core an agent is given
whole. An editor's preview follows a style or text edit with no reload.
And a run of fixes to what a running page reads while a change is still
going on.

items.text:
**A `writing-webfluent` skill for coding agents.** Agents that read
Agent Skills (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Zed and others)
can install one skill that teaches the loop: ask the compiler what a
component, store or token is before writing, then check, explain, fix,
format, test and verify. It names the mistakes models make most, each
with its code. References an agent reads by task go with it: code
quality and a review checklist; recipes (one small app in fifteen
pieces); styling (the tokens, themes, right to left); testing;
diagnostics (each common code, its cause and fix); PDFs, decks and
server rendering; and apps with Tauri for the desktop and the phone (the
typed bridge script, capabilities by platform, safe areas, Android's
back gesture, signing). A test compiles every example in them with no
warning, and checks that every command and code they name is one `wf`
has. The README says how to install it.

**`wf init` gives every new project the skill**, in `.agents/skills/`
and `.claude/skills/`; its language reference points at the project's
`AGENTS.md` rather than repeating it.

**The reference has a part for agents.** `AGENTS.md` gains "For
agents": the grammar in a few lines, ten idioms, the mistakes made most
(`T06`, `C02`, `X05`, `T13`, `E002`, `T17`) and one whole page; every
example compiles with no warning.

**`AGENTS.md` covers Tauri and Electron apps**, on the desktop and the
phone.

**Eleven icons for a design tool**: `pointer`, `reach`, `frame`,
`line`, `pipette`, `comment`, `hand`, `zoom`, `ruler`, `eye-off` and
`unlock`.

**PDFs and decks draw the logical insets** (`inset-inline`,
`inset-block`), read left to right as the logical paddings already were.

**`webfluent::patch`**: `in_place` compares two programs and answers
with what a running page must change to follow a style or text edit
(one class swapped and its rules, or an element's new text), or a
rebuild and why. `in_place_with` takes the project's breakpoints, and
`agrees` holds a patch to what a full build generates.

**Style values**: the logical pairs (`padding-inline`, `margin-block`,
`inset-inline`, …) are a `Pair` shape, and `grid-column`/`grid-row` a
`Placement`, each printed in the fewest words and edited one side or
line at a time; `cell`, `read_placement` and `edit_placement` are what a
drop in a grid writes.

A token set by `theme.tokens` carries that value, so an editor can say
the config overrides the theme's own. A theme's view can be of a theme
the project declares other than the one the config selects.

An agent's prompt prints the config with its keys sorted at every
depth, so one project always reads the same and keeps the prompt cache.
`ChangeSet` is `Clone`, and `absorb_reads` takes back what a copy read.

An editor's preview is no longer compressed, which took most of a warm
build's time.

**A cached request that fails no longer leaks an unhandled rejection.**
A `resource` with `cache:` whose request failed reported an uncaught
error beside the failure its `error` arm handled.

**A derived value read while a change is running is up to date.** An
action an effect called, which wrote a state and then read a derived
value of it, got the value from before its write.

**A change runs its effects oldest first**, so a branch that leaves
disposes of what it drew before any of it reads again; before, an
attribute could throw on the null and keep the branch from leaving. One
effect that throws no longer keeps the others from running.

**A store's derived values are worked out with the other stores in
reach**, in a test's render and a page rendered at build time, where a
derived value reading another store came out empty.

**`mod+shift+/` matches.** With Shift, a punctuation key sends its other
character, and `keyIs` refused it; it is now read by its place.

A locale whose file is not JSON says why, with the line and column,
instead of reading as a file with no messages.

**The reference says what the compiler does.** Every example in
`AGENTS.md` compiles: the `Row`, `Grid` and `Stack` rows wrote
`gap: md` (`T13`), key rule 20 wrote a deck in WebFluent 2 syntax, and
others bound `query`, named a loop `t`, used tokens no theme declares or
bound a `DatePicker` to a string. It counts 83 icons (it said 32 and 72,
as did the guide), gives the runtime's current sizes (2 of 41 modules,
6.8 kB gzipped for a static page), lists `E119`, `V12` and `I05` as the
warnings they are, adds rows for `E005` and `T22`, and documents
`wf render`, six CLI flags, `theme.dark`, `theme.builtin: "structural"`
and `i18n.literals`. `wf init` writes this reference into a new project,
so only a `wf` of this release gives a project the corrected one.

sections.intro: Nothing to change: run `wf check`.

summary:
A project written in Arabic, and translated by its own words: names in
any script, every string a reader sees looked up by the text as written,
plural forms chosen by the number in the text, and a locale that names its
digits. Every name a program binds is now its own, whatever the generated
code or the browser calls its own things. And the guide is rewritten,
chapter by chapter, by what a reader is there to do.

items.text:
**Translate a project by its own words** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/translate-by-the-words.md)).
With `"literals": true` in `i18n`, every string a reader sees (an
element's text, its `label:`, `title:`, `placeholder:`, `aria-label:`
and `alt:`, a record's text field, a value whose name says it is words,
such as `caretText` or `emptyLabel`) is looked up in the locale's table
by the text as written, and the source stays in the language it was
written in. A string that splices a value is one key, with a placeholder
named after it; Markdown written in place and a control's `labels:` are
words too. `wf test` translates the program as the build does. What no
table can translate (a text splicing more than a name) is the new
warning `I05`, where it is shown.

**Plural forms by the number in the text** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)).
A message with plural forms and exactly one number among its values
takes its form by that number, so `Text("{files} files")` reads right
in Arabic's two, few and many. With two numbers none is guessed.

**A locale may name its digits** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/translate-a-site.md#switch-the-locale)).
`setLocale("ar-u-nu-arab")` reads the `ar` table and writes `format`,
`ago` and every count in Arabic-Indic digits; `ar-u-nu-latn` is 0–9
whatever the browser would pick. A date pattern's figures follow, and
`a` is AM or PM in the locale's words. The document's `lang` stays the
language, so a stylesheet's `[lang="ar"]` still matches.

**`t()` in a store**, and `setLocale()` with it, where both compiled to
calls the page could not find.

**Names in any script** ([chapter 9](/learn/04-language-basics#naming)).
A program's own names start and go on as Unicode's UAX #31 says, with
the marks of their letters, and are one name however they were typed:
`state عددٌ = 3`, `store المهام`, `action أضف`. The editor grammar
reads them the same way. A bidirectional embedding, override or isolate
control in the source, which draws code one way while it runs another,
is the new warning `E119`.

**Markdown draws GFM tables** ([chapter 27](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)),
the same at build time and in the browser: a header row, a delimiter row
whose colons align each column, and `\|` for a pipe inside a cell.

**`Frame(srcdoc: html, sandbox: "")`** ([chapter 21](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md))
is a declared prop, where it was an attribute passed through with a
`C04` warning. A value that reads state is followed, so the frame
redraws as it changes.

**A picture may carry itself**: a `data:image/…` address on an `Image`'s or an `Avatar`'s `src:`, a Markdown picture or a sanitized `` is kept, in the live page, the pre-render and the template engine alike. A link, a frame, a form, and any `data:` that is not an image, are still refused.

**Fourteen icons** ([chapter 21](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/show-an-icon.md)), 72 in all:
`code`, `monitor`, `git-commit`, `play`, `layers`, `insert`, `grid`,
`list`, `square`, `pill`, `image`, `sparkle`, `lock` and `type`. An icon
drawn in the browser now carries `data-icon`, as a pre-rendered one did,
so a style keyed on the name matches both.

**WebP is lossy at `build.media.quality`** ([chapter 42](/reference/config#build-media)),
through libwebp, keeping alpha: a 23 kB PNG that came out as 189 kB of
WebP is now 5 kB. A file that would be no smaller than its original is
not written, and `wf assets --plan` says which widths were dropped.

**`output_type: "static"` pre-renders every page**, as `ssg: true`
does. The config accepted it and built a single-page app.

sections.title: For tools
sections.intro:
Each is for a tool built on the compiler
([chapter 41](/reference/cli#building-a-tool-on-the-compiler)); paths
are under `webfluent::`.

items.text:
**`agent::edit`** replaces each `old_text` where it is found exactly
once: exactly, then ignoring line endings, then the indent, then with
typographic quotes and dashes read as ASCII. Text found twice names its
lines, text found nowhere the three nearest, and the edits apply all or
none. `ChangeSet::edit` makes them on a file the set has read, and
refuses one that moved since; a missing file is `WebFluentError::NotFound`.
`ChangeSet::edited` shows what the edits would make of a file, before
and after, without changing the set, and `ChangeSet::dir` names the
project's folder.

**A change set over newer buffers**: it can be laid over buffers that
moved on, keeping what it wrote and read, and hands back a file's text
without its own change, for writing the hunks a reader accepted. It
never reaches outside the project through a link.

**Editing a style block's nested rules**: `SetRuleStyle` and
`RemoveRuleStyle` reach an `@media` or `&:state` rule, making it when
there is none. `SetStyle` and `AppendChild` keep the block as it is
written, and `SetProp` on `Card.elevated` writes the prop before the
flags, where it wrote a call that did not parse.

**`Template::with_studio`** writes each element's node id on what it
draws (`data-wf-node`, `data-wf-call`), as the builds do for an editor.

**A preview's resources held in an arm**: `data-wf-resource="loading"`
or `"error"` on a page's root makes every resource read as in that arm.

**`contrast::ratio`** is public, and a theme's view names as unpaired
every colour token the dark theme leaves alone, not only `color-*`.

**`wf commands --json`** reads each value's kind in a release build,
where it said every path was text.

**A program's names are its own wherever it binds them.** A loop's item,
a lambda's parameter, a `let`, a caught error, an action, a `const`, a
store or a service named like the generated code's own things (`_p`,
`e`, `event`, `document`) or a browser global (`Map`, `Set`, `Node`,
`setTimeout`) used to read the wrong value or stop the page from
drawing: `for e in entries { Link(to: "/e/{e.id}") }` went to
`/e/undefined`, and `const Map = 3` threw before any page drew. Each is
now spelt apart in the generated code, and the build's read-back of its
own JavaScript (`E901`) catches a clash that slips past.

**A component call's handlers and attributes follow its root** when the
body's `if` or `match` draws a new one: a button wrapped in a tooltip
while disabled kept its click once enabled.

**A state may start from a derived value defined before it**, where it
threw as the page drew.

**A derived function works everywhere**: the pre-render, `wf test` and
`wf render` painted every call to `derived countOf = (id) => …` blank,
inside a lambda too.
**A select keeps its value when its options are redrawn.**
**A modal reopened before its close event arrives stays open.**

**A drag whose first move leaves its element still begins**, in WebKit
too, and a draggable element selects no text.

**A shortcut on a punctuation key is found by its place** on a layout
that types no ASCII there, so `mod+,` works on an Arabic keyboard.
**A name narrowed out of null may still be set to null.**

**A member or field that does not exist is reported at its name**
(`T06` underlines `x`, not the store), so the build and the editor agree.

**`V01` offers the dot for a flag written without it**
(`Button(primary)`), and no longer matches a two-letter word to any
short name.
**`F04` no longer warns** about a checkbox that is always disabled.

**A binding that runs again with its value writes nothing**, the
browser asks about reduced motion once, and a windowed list fed an item
at a time lays out once a frame, revealing after it is laid out.

**A test's settle waits as long as it asks**, not two seconds each, and
an `expect` reads a page still moving again until it holds, for up to
a second and a half. A file of fifteen browser tests went from two
minutes to eighteen seconds.

**A test file's declaration named like one of the project's** is `E102`
where the tests are collected, where every browser test failed with a
SyntaxError.

**A prop that reads a store named like a browser global is followed**,
not copied once.

**A fix's word search no longer panics** on a character it would end
inside.

**Chart and QrCode are in the Data display group**, so a list of the
registry by group draws it once.

sections.title: The guide
sections.intro:
Every chapter is rewritten to a house style drawn from a study of
developer documentation, and the chapters are ordered by what a reader is
there to do: start, learn the language, build the parts of an app, ship,
and look things up. The site has a front page that answers a visitor's
questions in order, and its pages, sidebar and search come from the guide.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
See [chapter 51](/errors/upgrading#5-12): store members named like
an object's own (`E118`), a test declaration named like the project's
(`E102`), where `T06` is reported, `output_type: "static"`, and smaller
WebP. Run `wf check`.

summary:
What an editor written in WebFluent asked of the language: a handler that
reads every value an event sends, gestures on a component's call, a
modal's own heading and close button, source maps, a translated
`wf init`, and icons; and tests that find a control by the name a reader
hears, each test file with its own declarations.

items.text:
**A handler names each value its event sends** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#emitting-events-from-components)).
A component that declares `event menu(key: String, x: Number, y: Number)`
and `emit menu(k, x, y)` is handled with `on menu(key, x, y) { … }`, each
name typed as the event declares it. A handler may name fewer values
than the event sends, never more: a name past the last one is the new
error T22, which says what the event sends. The same holds for an api's
hooks and a connection's handlers.

**Gestures on a component's call** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#gestures-drag-long-press-swipe-and-the-splitter)).
`drag:`, `dragGroup:`, `dropValue:`, `dropAxis:`, `dropInside:`,
`on receive(d)`, `on dragmove(d)`, `on longpress` and `on swipe` written
on a component's call land on its root element, as `class:` and
`on contextmenu` already did. A component whose body is not one element
has nothing for them to land on, which is the new error C07.

**`Modal.Title` and `.closable`** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#overlays-modals-dialogs-toasts-and-menus)).
`Modal.Title { … }` (and `Dialog.Title`) is drawn in the heading in place
of `title:`'s words, so a heading can set a name apart in code;
`title:` stays the dialog's name. `.closable` puts a close button,
named Close, in the heading row. It closes the dialog as Escape does, so
`on close` runs and `visible:` follows. Both work in the live page, the
pre-render and the template engine.

**Source maps** ([chapter 39](/reference/config)).
`build.sourcemap` was in the config and nothing read it. It now writes a
version 3 map beside the bundle and each page's chunk (`app.js.map`,
`pages/Home.js.map`), with the sources' text, so a stack trace reads
back to the `.wf` line each statement came from. The scripts are
otherwise byte for byte what they are without one.

**`wf init --locales`** ([chapter 38](/reference/cli#wf-init)).
`wf init my-app --locales en,ar` (spa or static, the default first)
starts a project translated: the i18n config and `meta.lang`, every
visible string of the starter through `t()`, a language switch built
from the locales, and `src/translations/<locale>.json` for each. A tag
that is not one, a tag named twice and an empty list are refused, and so
are locales for `pdf` and `slides`.

**Three icons** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)), 58 in all:
`locate` for a panel that follows the caret, `folder-off` for a folder
that is gone, and `file-plus` for New file.

sections.title: For tools
sections.intro:
Each is for a tool built on the compiler
([chapter 38](/reference/cli#building-a-tool-on-the-compiler)); paths
are under `webfluent::`.

items.text: **`VERSION`**: the compiler's version, as `wf --version` prints it.

**`BuildOptions::sourcemap`** asks for maps whatever the config says,
for an editor's preview, and `codegen::sourcemap::SourceMap` reads a
map back and looks a place up, as a console does with a stack trace.

**`init::create_with(dir, name, &Options { template, locales })`** is
`wf init` with locales; `init::create` stays the form without them.

**The language server knows a handler's names**: hover gives each its
type and completion offers them, where hovering `e` in
`on click(e) { … }` used to show nothing. The tree-sitter grammar reads
several names.

**A test finds a control by the name a reader hears** ([chapter 24](/learn/16-testing#write-a-test-that-acts)).
What is `aria-hidden` (a menu item's shortcut, a glyph) is left out of
a name, so `click "Paste"` finds an item that shows Ctrl+V. A submenu's
entry is named by its label, not by its items: `WF.submenu` points the
entry's `aria-labelledby` at its label, for a screen reader and for
`click "File"`.

**A test file's declarations are its own.** Every test page was built
with every test file's declarations, so two files under `tests/` that
each declared `const T06` broke every test that runs in a browser
("Identifier 'T06' has already been declared"). A test now renders and
runs with the project's declarations and its own file's only.

**A closable modal's close button writes its state at once.** The state
followed a task later, with the `close` event, so opening the modal
again straight after closing it did nothing.

**A store's action named like a helper is the store's own.**
`OpenFiles.preview(path)`, called from another store's action, compiled
to the runtime's file preview and lost its argument. A value with a
method of its own named like a list or string helper (`last`, `first`,
`take` …) now answers for itself, with every argument.

**A block handed to a component reads the names where it was written**
in `wf test` and the template engine, as the live page and the
pre-render already did: a panel's `empty` text, handed to a frame with
an `empty` flag of its own, came out as "false".

**A `Menu.Item`'s `class:` is added beside the item's own**, where it
wrote over `wf-menu__item` and the item lost its padding and its
shortcut column.

**A15 holds a control's label to its words**, not to a glyph beside them
that the author marks `aria-hidden` (`Aa` beside "Match case").

**The components reference** has an example of `Modal.Title`,
`.closable` and `Dialog.Title`, so every part the registry lists has
one a tool can show.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
See [chapter 46](/errors/upgrading#5-11): gestures on a component
that is not one element (C07), a handler's names (T22), a test file's own
declarations, a control's name as a reader hears it, a block's names, a
menu item's class, and a value's own method over a helper. Run `wf check`.

summary:
The `wf init` starters, rewritten to work on first use, and the compiler
and runtime bugs that clicking through them turned up; what an editor
built on the compiler asks of it — icons, events, a member's `///`, a
build of one route, a faster check; and a pre-render, a test and a PDF
that draw what the live page draws.

items.text:
**Starters that work on first use** ([chapter 38](/reference/cli#wf-init)).
`wf init spa` has `Day` and `Night` themes with a switch that calls
`setTheme`, a task list that adds a task on Enter through a `Form` and
asks in a `Modal` before deleting one, a Settings page with validated
fields, and `tests/app.wf` and `tests/tasks.wf`. `wf init static` has a
validated contact form with a required agreement `Checkbox`, English and
Arabic translations, and `tests/site.wf`. `wf test` passes in a new
project.

**A test can place a whole page** ([chapter 24](/learn/16-testing#test-a-whole-page))
by its name, as it places a component (`Tasks`, then `click "Add"`),
with its state, stores and handlers running. This works for a page with
no route parameter whose name no component also has. In a test that
acts, `press "Enter"` in a form's text field submits the form, and
`click "Name"` also finds, by its name, an element whose role is a link,
a tab, a menu item (a `Menu.Item`), an option, a tree item, a switch, a
checkbox or a radio ([chapter 24](/learn/16-testing#write-a-test-that-acts)).

**`on blur` and `on focus` on a page** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#shortcuts-for-an-app)).
A page, a component or `app` hears the window lose and gain focus for as
long as it shows, for example to save when the window is left. Both
listen on the window; `on keydown` and `on keyup` still listen on the
document.

**`on auxclick`, `on focusin` and `on focusout` on any element**
([chapter 37](/reference#on-every-element)).
`on auxclick(e)` hears a click with a button other than the main one
(`e.button == 1` is the middle button, to close a tab); `on focusin` and
`on focusout` hear focus move onto or off the element or anything inside
it.

**23 icons for editors and tools** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)),
55 in all: `folder`, `folder-plus`, `file`, `refresh`, `alert-circle`,
`clock`, `dot`, `diff`, `book`, `git-branch`, `git-pull-request`, `pin`,
`more-horizontal`, `window-minimize`, `window-maximize`, `outline`,
`help-circle`, `collapse-all`, `chevron-up`, `globe`, `external-link`,
`panel-down` and `panel-up`. They go wherever an icon name does and are
drawn in `currentColor`.

**`Menu.Item.danger`** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)),
or `danger: true`, draws an item that cannot be undone, such as Delete
or Discard, in the danger colour.

**A `Tooltip`'s `shortcut:` reaches its control**
([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)):
`Tooltip("Save", shortcut: "mod+s") { Button("Save") }` also gives the
button `aria-keyshortcuts` in ARIA's spelling (`Control+S`, or
`Meta+S` on Apple's systems), unless it has one.

**A member's `///` is its documentation** ([chapter 5](/learn/04-language-basics#naming)).
A `///` comment above a `state`, `persist`, `derived` or `action` in a
page, a component or a store stays with it, in `.wf` and `.wfx` alike;
the parser used to drop it. A `///` above anything else in a body is
still dropped.

**`Portal`** ([chapter 32](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)).
`Portal(into: node) { … }` draws its block into a node somebody else's
code made: an editor's tooltip, a map's popup, a chart's legend. The
library keeps the node's place, its keys and its focus; the page keeps
what is in it. `into:` takes an element, a `ref:` handle or null; named
another node the block moves there with its state, and null keeps it
aside. Its handlers, `emit` and lifetimes belong to where it is written.
`Portal` is now a built-in's name, so a project's own component or store
of that name is reported.

**`Markdown(text).inert`** ([chapter 37](/reference/markdown)),
for text somebody else wrote, such as a language server's documentation:
entities are decoded and shown as text, a link is its words and a
picture is left out.

sections.title: For tools
sections.intro:
Each is for a tool built on the compiler
([chapter 38](/reference/cli#building-a-tool-on-the-compiler)); paths
are under `webfluent::`.

items.text:
**A build of one route.** `BuildOptions::only_route` (`Some("/posts/hello")`)
renders the page answering that route, for a preview that cannot wait
for a whole build. With a `BuildCache`, a page the cache holds for its
current inputs, in memory or on disk, is reused (`pages_reused`); any
other page this session has painted is written as it was last painted
and counted in the new `BuildReport::pages_deferred`; a page never
painted is rendered. The next build without the option renders what was
deferred, and its output equals a build from nothing. Without a cache it
builds everything, and what was last painted is kept only in memory, so
a `BuildCache::on_disk` reopened in a new session defers nothing.

**A member's documentation in the tree.** `StateDecl`, `DerivedDecl`
and `ActionDecl` carry `doc: Option<String>`, the `///` lines joined with
`\n`; `Statement::doc()` and `Statement::set_doc()` read and set it, for
a completion or a hover to show. `print::statement` writes a documented
member under its `///`, so a store whose members are documented prints
back as itself. `reprint` and `edit::rewrite_declaration` replace, remove
and insert a member together with its `///`: a member taken out left its
doc to document the next one, and one put in at the front went between
the first member and its doc. `print::written_start(source, &statement)`
is public: where a statement is written from, its `///` when it has one.

**A code's guide entry.** `diagnostics::codes::guide_section(code)`
returns a diagnostic code's section of the Diagnostics chapter as
Markdown, without its heading (what `wf explain` prints after the
summary, before setting it for a terminal), or `None`. The code is
matched as given: `T06`, not `t06`.

**A test's steps outside Chrome.** `testing::step_script(what, name,
value)` returns the JavaScript expression a `click`, `type` or `press`
step evaluates in the page, which answers `"ok"`, `"none"` or
`"no-option"`, so an editor's own window can find controls as `wf test`
does.

**A rendered test in its locale.** `testing::render_test` takes the
locale as a fourth argument (`Tests::locale()` is the project's default,
or `en`), and `template::render_program_fragment_in(program, data,
messages, locale)` renders with that locale's plural rules.

**The framing decision.** `codegen::csp::frames_itself(&program)`,
`config::project::frame_options(&config)` (`"DENY"` or `"SAMEORIGIN"`)
and the `BuildConfig::frames_itself` flag, which the build fills in, so
a server an editor runs for its preview can send what `wf serve` sends.

**A starter's files.** `init::Template::files()` lists a starter's own
files, as (path, text) pairs with the project's name still `{{name}}`;
`init::create` writes them, and `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md` and `public/`
beside them.

**The registry** ([chapter 38](/reference/cli#wf-docs)):
`wf registry --json` lists the new icons, `auxclick`, `focusin` and
`focusout` among every element's events, and `danger` on `Menu.Item`.

**Paged layout.** `paged::style::Length::Mix(points, percent)` holds a
`calc()` of both (`calc(50% - 12px)` is `Mix(-9.0, 50.0)`); `Style` gains
`has_mix()` and `settle_mix(w, h, main)`; `codegen::builtin::span_class`
writes a `Column`'s span class.

**`check_project_via` runs its phases on scoped threads**, and calls a
`Project`'s `file_of` and `source_of` up front, on the calling thread.
The findings and their order are unchanged.

**A handler reads `key` and `value`** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#the-event-object)).
`on keydown { if key == "Enter" { … } }` passed the check and threw
`ReferenceError: key is not defined` on the first key press, which broke
Enter in the SPA starter. A handler that reads `key` now gets
`event?.key`, and one that reads `value` gets `event?.target?.value`, on
every kind of handler; a state, a loop item or a parameter of that name
is left alone.

**A layer that starts open no longer stops the page drawing**
([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)).
A `Modal`, `Dialog`, `Popover` or state-opened `Menu` whose `visible:`
was `true` from the start asked to open before it was in the document,
and threw; each now opens once it is there. A layer anchored to an
element stayed clamped to the window's edge once the element scrolled
away; it now hides with it (`data-anchor-hidden`), stays open and shows
again when the element comes back. The Escape that closes an open
`Modal` or `Dialog` no longer reaches the page behind it.

**Menus and tooltips** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)).
`Menu(label:)` is the list's accessible name; the button's words come
from `trigger:` (a `Dropdown`'s still from `label:`), so a menu that
`visible:` opens no longer draws a stray button. Each menu and each
tooltip drawn gets its own id at run time (`WF.uid`), where every copy a
`for` or a component drew shared one, so `aria-controls` and
`aria-describedby` could name another copy's. A menu keeps its `class:`
and its `style { }` class as it opens and closes.

**Forms ask their rules** ([chapter 16](/learn/14-forms#choose-when-a-message-shows)).
A `Form` with no `bind:` in a page or component with `validate` rules
ran `on submit` anyway; it now stops on a failing rule and shows the
messages. Each page and each copy of a component has its own form
handles: a page's carried into the next page compiled, and every copy of
a component shared one form. A validated `Checkbox` or `Switch` shows
its message beneath it, announced and tied to the control
(`aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`). A field's character count follows
a value the program sets, such as a reset.

**Controls given a value work** ([chapter 16](/learn/14-forms#bind-a-control-to-state)).
`Switch(checked: value)` without `bind:` drew no input; it now follows
the value, and its `on change` hears the click. A `Switch`'s `on change`
was never attached. A bound `Checkbox` or `Radio` with its own
`on change` lost the binding's write; the binding now writes first and
the handler runs after it.

**Text that reads state follows it** ([chapter 21](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)).
Each of these was worked out once, when the page was drawn: the labels
of `Checkbox`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Slider`, `DatePicker` and
`FileUpload`; a `Table`'s `caption:`; `Tabs.Page` titles; `Tooltip`
text; a `Modal`'s or `Dialog`'s `title:`; a `Menu`'s `trigger:` and a
`Dropdown`'s `label:`; an `Avatar`'s `src:`, `alt:` and `initials:`; a
`Skeleton`'s `width:`, `height:` and `size:`; and an `Icon`'s positional
name (`Icon(if done { "check" } else { "clock" })`). So
`Checkbox(label: t("…"))` now changes language with `setLocale`. Fixed
text compiles as before.

**Stores** ([chapter 12](/learn/11-stores)). A
store outlives the page that reads it first: its derived values and
effects belonged to that page's scope and stopped when the reader moved
on. A `derived` that reads one written below it in the same store
follows it, where it kept its first value. The built script declares
each store after the stores it `use`s, so a read made while the script
starts never meets a store not declared yet.

**The pre-render paints what the live page draws**
([chapter 26](/about/static-or-single-page#what-the-static-paint-knows)).
A `Checkbox`, `Radio` or `Switch` is its `<label>` and `<input>`, ticked
and disabled as its state starts, where only the labels' words showed.
A `Menu` or `Dropdown` is its button and a hidden list, where its
entries lay in the page, and a menu that state opens is its list alone.
A part written with flags carries their
classes (`Menu.Item.danger`), and `Column(span: 8)` its `wf-col--8`,
where every column was painted the same width. `disabled`, `required`
and `controls` are written only when `true`, here and in the template
engine, so `Button("Go", disabled: false)` is not a dead button.
`.pop()` and `.shift()` are evaluated on a list the build knows.

**A test that looks reads the page as a reader does**
([chapter 24](/learn/16-testing#write-a-test-that-looks)). The template
engine draws a `Menu` or `Dropdown` as its button and hidden list,
`keyLabel("mod+shift+p")` as the build writes it (`Ctrl+Shift+P`), and
a `t()` with a count in the default locale's CLDR form. `expect` decodes
every numeric entity and the common named ones, so `expect "It isn't"`
matches. In a test that acts, `expect` treats any run of white space as
one space, as a test that looks already did.

**Column spans leave room for the gap** ([chapter 37](/reference/column)).
`span: 8` and `span: 4` in a `Row` with a gap came to 100% plus the gap,
and the second always wrapped; each span now gives up its share of the
gap, a gap or a span given per breakpoint too. A PDF lays a
`Column` out at its `span:`, where every column came out equal, and the
PDF engine's `calc()` is a real parser: no spaces needed, nested
parentheses, unary minus, functions inside, and a sum of a percentage
and points resolved against the box it lands in
([chapter 34](/learn/17-pdf-and-slides#the-paged-engine)).

**The `Navbar` follows the theme** ([chapter 37](/reference/navbar)).
Its background was a fixed translucent white; it is now the theme's
surface, and its text the theme's text colour.

**`setLocale` is remembered** ([chapter 21](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md))
across page loads, in `localStorage` under `wf:locale`, so a static site
keeps the reader's language from page to page. A `?lang=` address still
wins, without changing the saved choice.

**A site may frame its own pages** ([chapter 23](/about/security#the-content-security-policy)).
A `Frame` whose `src:` is site-relative (`"/preview/"`, `"/embed/{id}"`)
was refused by the site's own headers. A project that places one is
served `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` by `wf serve`, and its `_headers`
says the same with `frame-ancestors 'self'`; every other project keeps
`DENY` and `'none'`.

**An `Avatar`'s `src:` is checked** like any other `src:`
([chapter 23](/about/security#what-the-compiler-guarantees)): a
run-time value goes through `WF.safeUrl`.

**Long keyed lists no longer stall as they grow**
([chapter 20](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)). A keyed `for` read the place
of every item it kept before each change, so a 960-line log appended
line by line froze the page for 3.5 s. Only items whose index changes
are measured now; a list that only grows at its end measures nothing.

**A `Splitter` moves from where it is drawn**
([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#gestures-drag-long-press-swipe-and-the-splitter)).
A drag or an arrow key starts from the region's drawn size, not the
bound value, and a reset writes `reset:` as given, so `reset: 0` can
mean the region's default share.

**`() => …` takes no arguments** ([chapter 14](/reference/expressions#fields-calls-and-methods)).
It was typed as taking one, so it could fail to fit a script parameter
whose JSDoc says `() => boolean`.

**`webfluent` on Windows** ([chapter 2](/learn/01-getting-started#windows-powershell)).
A bare `wf` runs `WF.msc`, the Windows Firewall console, which comes
first on `PATH`. The `.msi`, the release zip and `install.ps1` now also
install the binary as `webfluent.exe`, so `webfluent build` works;
`wf.exe` does too. The `.msi` now keeps one `UpgradeCode`, where each
release had its own, so the next one replaces it instead of installing
beside it. The Node binding looks for `webfluent.exe` and `wf.exe` by
their full names ([chapter 35](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)).

**The check does less** ([chapter 38](/reference/cli#wf-check)).
The `env` lint lexes only a file whose text could name `env.…`, and the
output checks work out what a build can evaluate only once they find a
`Chart` or a `QrCode`: on Halyard the check went from 28 ms to 18 ms.
Its phases also run side by side, which helps most on a busy machine.

**A build into another folder reuses the cache**
([chapter 38](/reference/cli#wf-build)). The cache's key held the
output folder, so two builds of one project into different folders, as
an editor's previews are, never shared a page.

**Markdown links are checked, and backslash escapes work**
([chapter 27](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)). Every link and
picture in `Markdown` goes through the scheme check the rest of a page
does, so `[x](javascript:…)` is drawn as its words. A backslash before
punctuation draws that character (`\*` is `*`, not emphasis), as
CommonMark has it, and the build and the browser draw Markdown alike,
line breaks and white space included.

**Escape goes to the newest layer that can take it**
([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)).
A tooltip under the pointer no longer takes Escape from the page (an
editor's completion list behind a toolbar button lost it); it hides and
lets the key go on. An open `Modal` or `Dialog` is the newest layer, so
its Escape comes before a popover's beneath it, and a press inside it no
longer closes that popover. `on close` on a modal is its event, with no
`V09`.

**Every built-in takes what any element takes**
([chapter 37](/reference)). `role:`,
`tabindex:`, `aria-*`, `data-*` and `on` handlers reached a `Popover`,
`Menu`, `Tooltip`, `Modal`, `VirtualList`, `Splitter`, `Tabs`,
`Sidebar`, `Slider` and the rest only in part, or not at all; each now
writes them on its element, in the live page, the pre-render and the
template engine alike, as `C04` says. `disabled: true` disables a
`Slider`, `DatePicker` or `FileUpload`. An `html:` written on an element
is an attribute, never markup.

**A long list drawn before its box is laid out**
([chapter 37](/reference/virtuallist)) paints the
right rows in its first frame, the row `reveal:` names among them, where
it drew about forty and trimmed them a frame later.

**A pre-rendered modal** has its title as its heading, as the live page
draws it, not as a `title=` tooltip; an `IconButton`'s own `title:` wins
over its label on every page.

**A test reads a page as a reader does**
([chapter 24](/learn/16-testing#write-a-test-that-looks)). `expect` reads
a plain render as a browser lays it out: elements that touch read as
touching, where the render's line breaks put a space between them. A
test run in a browser loads the project's own stylesheets and serves
`public/` beside the page, as the built page does.

**A record with all its fields defaulted is `Offers()`**
([chapter 12](/learn/11-stores#a-first-store)), wherever an
expression goes, a prop's default among them; a left-out field of a
default record is filled in, in the pre-render too.

**`data-x: true` is `data-x="true"`** on every page, given to an element
or passed through a component's call, and a call's `data-*`, `aria-*`,
`id:` and `class:` reach the component's root in the template engine.

**A local is its own** ([chapter 12](/learn/11-stores#actions)). A
`let`, a parameter or a loop's name in a store's action that shares a
member's name was compiled to the member, so writing it wrote the store;
in a page or a component, one that shared a prop's name read the prop.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
See [chapter 46](/errors/upgrading#5-10): Markdown's backslash
escapes and checked links, attributes that built-ins now write, a modal's
Escape and painted title, column spans that leave room for the gap, a `Menu`'s `label:` that no longer names its button, a
form without `bind:` that asks its rules, a bound box whose `on change`
wrote the value itself, and pre-rendered HTML and test snapshots that now
match the live page are what a project may notice. On Windows, type
`webfluent` and uninstall an older MSI. Run `wf check`.

summary:
An app's frame — layers, shortcuts, gestures, long lists, workers, frames —
and the compiler as a library an editor, a visual builder or an agent
builds on, each piece also a `wf` command.

items.text:
**Layers** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#layers-popovers-menus-and-tooltips-above-everything)). `Popover`, a `Menu` at
its button, at an anchor or at a point (`at:`, for a context menu), with
submenus, and `Tooltip`, drawn in the browser's top layer, so nothing
clips or covers them. Each flips and slides to stay on screen; Escape
closes the top one, a press outside closes what it is outside of, and
focus goes back where it was.

**Shortcuts for an app** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#shortcuts-for-an-app)). `mod` is ⌘
on Apple's systems and Ctrl elsewhere; chords (`"mod+k mod+s"`);
`keyIs(e, …)` and `keyLabel(…)` for a table of commands that drives
menus and a palette; a page, a component or `app` hears `keydown` and the
window's events itself; `trapFocus` keeps focus inside a panel.

**Gestures** ([chapter 9](/learn/08-events#gestures-drag-long-press-swipe-and-the-splitter)). `drag:` and
`on receive(d)` with a ghost, edge scroll and Escape; `on longpress`,
`on swipe`; and `Splitter` between two regions, with its size kept.

**`VirtualList`** ([chapter 37](/reference)): a
long list drawn a window at a time, rows measured or of a fixed height,
`reveal:` to scroll one into view, and `V12` for a long list that is
not windowed.

**`worker`** ([chapter 18](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)): a Web Worker held
like a connection, asked with `.request(method, params)` and heard with
`on message`, restarted when it crashes; a store may hold connections.

**`Frame`** ([chapter 28](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)): another page inside
this one, its `on message` only that page's; `A17` for a frame with no
title.

**`persist` follows its key** ([chapter 12](/learn/11-stores)):
`key: Project.id` keeps one value per project; `in: .app` names a
storage the project gives itself, which may answer later.

**The policy names an app's own schemes and WebAssembly**
([chapter 33](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)): `meta.connect` and
`meta.frame` take `ipc:` or `wfpreview:`, `meta.wasm` lets a page compile
WebAssembly, `meta.style_elements` lets a script write `<style>`.

**A build cache**: only the pages an edit changed are pre-rendered
again, in a session (`BuildCache::in_memory`) or across runs.

**An `Image`'s literal `src:` in `public/` is processed** as an `image`
declaration is: each width and format, its size, a `<picture>`.

**Previews of what a reader asked for**: `data-wf-motion="reduce"` on
the page's root stills every animation as `prefers-reduced-motion` does,
and `data-wf-validation="shown"` shows every field's message as a failed
submit does.

**Plurals by CLDR** ([chapter 21](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)): the build picks
each count's form by the default locale's rules (CLDR 48, the same
table the browser's `Intl.PluralRules` reads), and exactly none is
`key.zero` in any language.

sections.title: For tools
sections.intro:
Every one reads the project through a `Vfs`, so an editor's unsaved
buffers count ([chapter 38](/reference/cli#building-a-tool-on-the-compiler)).

items.text:
**Printing and reprinting**: `webfluent::print`, `reprint` and
`edit::rewrite_*` change an element, a statement or a declaration in the
tree and write the smallest edit, every other byte as it was.

**The node map both ways**: each element's id, place, parent and what it
is inside; the node at a caret; the Layers tree; `wf build --studio`
stamps `data-wf-node` and writes `nodes.json`.

**Data an inspector draws from**, each a command too: `wf components`
(every component, built-in and the project's), `wf theme` (every token,
its uses and its contrast), `wf motion`, `wf rules` (the `validate`
rules, named patterns, every state's rules), `wf scope FILE:LINE` (what
can be read at a place, typed), `wf translations` (what each locale
lacks, what nothing names; `--plurals`), `wf assets`, `wf config`,
`wf commands`; and style values read into their parts and written back.

**`wf fix`**: one decided fix on every family that has a certain one,
and fix-all per family.

**An agent's change set and context**: `webfluent::agent` holds an
agent's edits apart from the working tree, builds them before anyone
reads them, and gives them back by file or by hunk; `wf context` is what
an agent is given — the files, the problems, the components, the theme,
the config with only its public `env`, and the guide.

A project's own animation (`Card(animate: .Drop)`) did nothing on an
element that stood still; it plays.

A refined type's open end (`Number(0..10)` took 10) and its `after:` and
`before:` were not checked as the reader typed.

Pre-rendered controls dropped `name:` and `autocomplete:`, and an
`Input` with its own `id:` got a second one, so its label named nothing.

A locale missing one plural form showed the default locale's form, two
languages on one page; a site whose default locale is right to left was
served left to right until a script ran; `ar-EG` was not right to left.

A `let` in an action, a handler, an effect or a timer was offered by
completion everywhere in its page, and listed as a store's member.

`I01` and `I02` missed a `t()` in a page's header; `I03` said a reader
sees the key, where they see the default locale's message.

`Unsafe.Html` without a `sanitize(…)` elsewhere put nothing in; a typo
was reported once per check that found it; a page's own `state env` read
the project's `env`.

A comma between two style declarations made the browser drop both; it is
an error.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
See [chapter 46](/errors/upgrading#5-9): a comma between style
declarations, a field that accepted its range's open end, an animation
that now plays, a `zero` message that now shows, and a right-to-left
default locale are what a project may notice. Run `wf check`.

summary:
A state that copies a live value says so, a script's values reach a page,
and the guide shows a project as a desktop app.

items.text:
**`X06`: a state that copies a live value once.** `state clock =
now(every: 1.seconds)` holds the moment the page opened and never ticks
again, so every «… ago» built from it freezes; the same holds for
`viewport`, `query`, `hash`, `theme`, `network` and `update`. The warning
names it where it is written, and when nothing assigns, binds or changes
the state, the quick fix declares it `derived`, which follows the live
value. A state the program does change — `state tab = query.tab ?? "all"`
that a click then sets — is a starting value on purpose and draws
nothing.

**Desktop apps, in the guide.** [Chapter 33](https://github.com/monzeromer-lab/WebFluent/blob/master/md-docs/recipes/index.md)
shows a project as a Tauri or an Electron app: the build settings a
desktop needs, setting up each shell, the dev loop, calling the native
side through typed functions in a script under `src/`, events, plugins,
the security policy and packaging. The chapters after it move up one,
to 34–49.

**A script's values reach a page.** A value a project script declares at
its top level — `const VERSION = "1"`, a `let`, a `var`, `window.ready =
…` — compiled to a signal read, `_VERSION()`, wherever a page or a
component read it: in text, a splice, a `derived`, an `if` or `show`
condition, an attribute, a handler. Nothing declares `_VERSION`, so the
page threw as it drew (`_VERSION is not defined`), and `wf check` passed.
A call to a script's function was right; a function handed on as a value
was not. Every name a script declares is now its own global, read as
itself, unless the page or component declares the same name, whose
state still wins.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Nothing to change. A function written only to get a script's value onto a
page can go back to being the value. A build may now warn `X06` on a
`state` whose first value reads a live one; making it `derived` is the
fix.

summary: A resource asked again for what it shows keeps it on the page.

items.text:
**A refresh keeps the page.** Every time a resource was asked again —
`on: .focus`, `on: .interval(…)`, `reload()`, `invalidate()` — it went
back to `loading`, so a `match` over it took the page down to its loading
arm and built the ready arm again: a skeleton flash, the scroll lost, the
focus and an open sheet gone, every row and every component in it new.
Asking again for the same request is now a refresh: the resource stays
`ready` and keeps its data while it runs, and the answer is drawn in
place. `loading` is for a first load — nothing has arrived yet — and for
a request that changed: an address or an argument that reads state now
names something else (another environment, another page number), where
what is on screen would be the wrong data.

**A refresh that fails keeps the data.** The resource stays `ready` and
sets `name.error`, which the next answer clears, so the ready arm can say
the data is stale (`if rows.error != null { Alert(…).warning }`). A first
load that fails is `error`, as it was.

**A `match` arm's binding is live.** `ready(d)` and `error(e)` were
handed their value once, when the arm was drawn. A read of the binding
now follows the resource: text, attributes, `if`, `if let`, a keyed `for
… by` and a component's props inside the arm change in place when a
refresh lands, and the arm is drawn again only when the arm itself
changes — loading, ready, error. An enum's arm follows a new payload of
the same case the same way (`.failed(r)` kept showing the first reason it
was drawn with), and `else` is one arm, whichever keys it stands for.

**An `if let` binding is live.** `if let u = selected { Sheet(u) }`
showed the value it was drawn with until `selected` went to null and
back; another value now reaches the branch in place.

**A keyed list keeps an item for as long as its key is in it.** An item
whose value changed under the same key — every row of a refreshed
response, which is all new objects — was built again, its focus and its
components' state with it. It now keeps its nodes, and its body reads the
item and the index live. A row a refresh did not change is not even
visited: what an answer has in common with the data shown is kept as the
same objects (an item matched by its `id`, or by its value, or by its
place), so an answer that changed nothing redraws nothing.

**`name.refreshing` and `name.pending`.** `refreshing` is true while a
refresh runs with the data still shown; `pending` is true while any
request of the resource runs, the first load included. Both are `Bool`s,
live wherever they are read. With `paginate:`, the next page is a
refresh: `loadMore()` keeps the gathered items on the page, and another
`loadMore()` while a page is on its way is ignored.

**`ready(users)` over `resource users` reads the data.** An arm's binding
named like its resource — the guide's own example — compiled to the
resource's handle, so `users.length` was undefined and `for user in
users` drew nothing.

**`on:` and `cache:` on a resource over an address are policies.**
`fetch("/api/rows", on: .focus)` handed the runtime the word `"focus"`,
so such a resource never looked again — on focus, on reconnect or on an
interval — and its `cache:` was not read as a policy either. They are
read as an endpoint's are.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Nothing to change. What a page did to live through a refresh can go: a
sheet or a form kept outside the `match` with a snapshot of the data, a
`derived` copy held so the arm would not draw again. A page that wants a
spinner on every refresh shows one for `name.refreshing`. A hand-written
`WF.match` arm is handed its value as before, and an accessor of it as a
second argument; `WF.each` keeps a keyed item's nodes under a new value
with `live: true`, which is what a compiled `for … by` asks for.

summary: What a branch inside a branch drew goes when the outer one does.

items.text:
**A branch takes everything it holds when it goes.** An `if`, `if let`,
`match` or `for` at the top of another's body — directly in it, not
inside an element — draws into the same parent as the outer one. The
outer one remembered the nodes it drew when it drew them and took only
those away, so what the inner one drew later stayed on the page:
`if let m = picked { if act == null { Sheet(m) } }` left the sheet
showing once `act` went back to null and then `picked` did, and a tab
whose `match` over a resource drew again on a refetch left its list
beside the next tab's. The same held for `if … else if … else` (the arm
drawn last stayed beside the first), for a keyed list item with an `if`
of its own (moved, and taken away, without what the `if` drew since),
for a list inside a list item, and for a scoped slot's fill. Each now
draws between two markers of its own and takes what lies between them,
as it is when it changes. Exit animations, and a pre-rendered page taken
over in place, work as they did.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Nothing to change. A wrapper written only to keep a nested branch apart —
a `Stack` styled `display: contents` around a tab's `match`, or a branch
flattened into one `if let` over a `derived` value — can go.

summary: Two things that compiled and then did not work in the browser.

items.text:
**A resource read in a label follows the resource.** Whether text or an
attribute is drawn live was decided by the reads a state compiles to, and
a resource's or a connection's values are read through its handle, so a
label that read only one was worked out once, while it was loading:
`Button(if plan.data != null { "Request approval" } else { "Deploy" })`
stayed "Deploy" after the plan arrived, and `Text("{rows.state}")` stayed
"loading". `name.state`, `.data`, `.error` and a connection's `.messages`
are now live in text, a splice and an attribute alike.

**A list's key may read the index.** `for e, n in list by n` threw before
the list drew (`_n is not defined`), and `wf check` passed: the key was
compiled with the item alone. It is given the item and the index, so `by
n` works and so does `by "{e.id}-{n}"` — though a key of the index alone
moves with the position, and keeps nothing across an insert.

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
Nothing to change. A `derived` value written only to make a resource's
label live can go back into the label.

summary: A name the language has is not a program's to declare.

items.text:
**A name the language already has is `E118`, where it is declared.** A
page's `state env` compiled every read to the build's settings and every
write to the state: `"{env}"` showed `[object Object]`, `env == "prod"`
was never true, and `wf check` said nothing. A loop's `t` hid the
translation function inside the loop the same way. Such a name is now
refused as a `state`, `derived`, `persist` or `let`, a prop, a route or
action parameter, a loop item, a lambda's parameter, a binding of `if
let`, `match` or a slot, and as a top-level `const`, `data`, `image`,
store or `api`. The names are `env`, `params`, `locale` and `dir`; the
values the browser keeps current (`now`, `viewport`, `query`, `hash`,
`theme`, `network`, `update`); the language's functions (`t`, `format`,
`ago`, `log`, `navigate`, `fetch`, `uuid`, `every`, `after`, …); the
words a statement is written with (`state`, `action`, `let`, `if`,
`show`, `match`, `style`, `on`, …); and, at the top level, the runtime's
`WF`. The message suggests a name of your own where there is a usual one
— `target` for `env`, `search` for `query`, `scheme` for `theme`.
`event`, `e`, `value`, `key` and the browser's globals stay yours, and so
does any name as a field, a map key or an enum case.

**A top-level `const env` is refused where it is written.** It was
refused only when the build read its own bundle back, as "a bug in
WebFluent" (`E901`).

sections.title: Upgrading
sections.intro:
A program that declares one of these names stops at `E118`, on the line
that declares it; rename it and its reads. The usual ones are a loop's or a
lambda's `t` (`for t in todos`, `items.filter(t => …)` — `todo`, `item`),
`state query` (`search`), `persist theme` (`scheme`), a route parameter or
`state env` (`target`, `stage`) and an action named `update` (`edit`). The
guide, the examples and the site were renamed the same way.

summary:
A service read from its OpenAPI document is typed as well as one written by
hand, and a browser run leaves nothing behind.

items.text:
**A string with cases is an `enum`.** `{"type": "string", "enum": ["prod",
"test"]}` — what utoipa writes for a Rust enum — was imported as an empty
record, so `Text("{e.env}")` showed `[object Object]` and drew `T20`. It is
now `enum Env { prod, test }`, whose cases are the strings the server sends.
When a case cannot be written as a name (`"operate.flags"`, a digit first,
`true`), the schema is a `String` wherever it is named.

**A value that may be null is `T?`, however the document says so.**
OpenAPI 3.1's `"type": ["string", "null"]` was `Any?`; it is `String?`, and
the same holds for numbers, booleans and lists. A `oneOf` (or `anyOf`) of
`{ "type": "null" }` and a `$ref` is that type's `?`, 3.0's
`"nullable": true` counts beside a `type`, an `allOf` or a `$ref`, and a
record or an enum whose own schema allows null is `T?` wherever it is named.

**`allOf` is a record that extends another.** `[{ "$ref": "…/EnvSummary" },
{ "properties": … }]` is `type ServerDetail = EnvSummary { … }`; a second
record it names and every part written in place are fields of its own, and
what the schema around a part requires, the part's fields answer to.

**A string's `format` is the language's type for what the server sends.**
`date-time` is a `DateTime`, `date` a `Date`, `uuid` a `Uuid`, `email` an
`Email`, `uri` a `Url` — in a response, and in every record only responses
reach. What the program sends (a parameter, a request body, and every
record one reaches, but for its `readOnly` fields) keeps `String`, so a
route parameter or an input's text can still be sent. `time` stays a
`String`: JSON Schema's carries an offset `Time` does not read.
